title: InformationEntity
description: A named logical category of information (e.g. customer PII, payment card data, medical records) defined independently of where or how it is stored, which carries a sensitivity classification and is the object to which InformationRights grant actors access. It names *what* the data is, not the endpoint, table or field that holds it. Use SecureResource instead when the protected thing is a concrete technical artefact (an API endpoint, database table, file store, service or UI) with operations performed on it, rather than a storage-independent category of data. Use DataClassification instead when you are modelling the classification scheme itself (levels, encryption obligations) rather than a specific data category that is assigned one of those levels. Use FieldAccessControl instead when the control applies to one named field and its masking or redaction strategy, rather than to a whole logical grouping of data that may span many fields and stores.

description.description: Free-text explanation of what data this information asset comprises (example fields, data subjects, and systems where it appears); set it whenever the entity name alone does not make the boundary of the asset clear.

classification.description: Sensitivity classification of this information asset. Use classificationLevel values: public, internal, confidential, restricted, or top-secret.

authorizationRequirements.description: References InformationRight nodes defining which actors may access this entity and under what constraints.

x-dr-standard: STS-ml Information entity; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 RA-2 (Security Categorization) and AC-3 (Access Enforcement)
x-dr-evidence: A data inventory, record-of-processing (ROPA) or data-catalog document listing named data categories such as 'Customer PII' or 'Cardholder Data', each with a sensitivity level.
An enum or constant set of data categories (e.g. DataCategory.PII, DataCategory.PHI, DataCategory.PCI) referenced by authorization checks or masking logic across several classes.

Marker annotations or catalog tags (e.g. @PersonalData(category="contact"), BigQuery policy tags, AWS Macie or Purview classifications) applied consistently to fields in multiple models or tables to group them into one asset.
